text.p: These are the leading stories in the Lebanese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- The government prepares fast development projects for Bekaa Valley area before July 4.

Former Hizbollah leader Sheikh Sobhi Tufaili has called on residents of the region to start a "hunger revolt" in the form of a civil disobedience campaign on July 4 to pressure the government into easing poverty.
- Two guerrillas were killed in clashes with the Israeli forces in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
- Shareholders in Lebanon's biggest company Solidere agreed to cancel shares worth $170 million, reducing the real estate firm's capital to $1.650 billion.
- France brushes aside Israeli reports that Paris will send troops to south Lebanon to replace the Israeli forces in Israel's south Lebanon occupation zone.
- Kuwait extends $33 million loan to Lebanon to finance a water supply project in Beirut.
- Lebanon's weekly treasury bill issue of June 26 raised 253.6 billion Lebanese pounds. The issue posted a nominal surplus of subscription against maturity of 61 billion pounds.
- Yields on short-term Lebanese treasury bills for the July 3 issue fell while long-term t-bill yields held steady.
- Prime Minister Hariri heads to Morocco for a three-day official visit.
